A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftShadow study, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF contains an appendix, although both refer to separate supplementary training details.

before.justification: v1 reports original shadow-removal results on SRD, ISTD+, LRSS, and UIUC, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative examples, and loss ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds mask-sensitivity results, another comparison method, and a pretrained-model control.

M1.justification: The reported central penumbra loss changes from separately rectified, signed horizontal and vertical derivatives in v1 Equations 5–6 to a rectified dot product between a normalized radial direction and the mask gradient in v2 Equations 7–8. These objectives are not generally equivalent. The SAM–LoRA architecture and other two losses remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use SRD, ISTD+, LRSS, and UIUC for image shadow removal, including transfer evaluation on LRSS and UIUC. The added mask-source comparisons operate within the existing ISTD+ task and image population.

E2.justification: v2 adds SG-ShadowNet to the SRD comparison in Table 1 and the qualitative comparison in Figure 1. Figure 1 also adds BMNet, while the corresponding SRD comparison in v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 5 gains Inpaint4Shadow.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a controlled ISTD+ comparison using GT, Otsu, BDRAR, FDRNet, and pretrained-SAM masks, plus an unfinetuned SAM–ShadowDiffusion control in the ablation. Newly stated resolution, optimizer, and dataset counts do not establish changes to existing experimental settings.

E4.justification: The new mask-sensitivity study systematically tests dependence on external mask quality, substantially extending the analysis beyond the earlier loss ablations. v2 also adds a pretrained-weights control to distinguish finetuning gains, revises qualitative cases, and retains the earlier penumbra evaluation and loss comparisons.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 introduces Mean and Std Dev rows for comparisons across mask sources. Neither version reports repeated-training counts, seeds, or run-based confidence intervals. The calculation underlying the new standard deviations is unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds SG-ShadowNet scores, mask-sensitivity results, and pretrained-control results, including PSNR 31.27 on SRD and 21.40 on LRSS. Previously reported numerical entries are retained, including SoftShadow's 35.57 SRD and 35.00 ISTD+ whole-image PSNR. Qualitative examples are also expanded or replaced.

T1.justification: v1's linear illumination derivation and its mask-gradient relation to penumbra width are removed. v2 instead formally defines a threshold-selected penumbra region, its centroid, and normalized radial directions under gradual-transition and gradient-direction assumptions. This substantially revises the mathematical basis of the central constraint.

C1.justification: The principal claims about soft masks, joint mask-free removal, performance, and generalization remain. However, v2's introduction removes the explicit claim of much lower computational cost than previous methods. Naming mask reconstruction in the abstract describes a loss already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explains sensitivity to external masks, qualifies its advantage on hard-shadow-heavy ISTD+, and acknowledges the LRSS SSIM decrease when adding the penumbra loss. It also gives a more affirmative interpretation of that loss's SRD benefit than v1, despite retaining the ablation scores.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 256×256 finetuning, the Adam optimizer, ISTD+ training/testing counts, and that evaluation penumbra regions use predicted soft masks. These are additional disclosures. Conversely, v1's repository-link footnote is omitted; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Style-guided Shadow Removal, Mask-ShadowGAN, and Adam, while removing the shadow-removal survey cited in v1. The main positioning relative to shadow removal, shadow detection, and SAM adaptation remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, and ablation discussion undergo substantial rewriting. Mask reconstruction moves into Section 3.2, and Section 5 becomes Framework Analysis, combining relocated penumbra evaluation with sensitivity analysis and ablations. The title and terminology are also revised.

P2.justification: The framework, shadow-formation, and constraint illustrations are redrawn. Qualitative panels are replaced or expanded and relocated, including additional comparator columns and examples. v2 adds the mask-sensitivity table, expands the ablation display, and changes the document template and caption formatting.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful sensitivity evidence, a pretrained control, clearer ablation labels, and implementation details. However, it replaces the central loss formula while retaining prior result values without explaining their relationship to the revised formulation. Table 4's new standard deviations, 0.912 and 0.993, also do not match the dispersion across its listed mask-condition scores, and their calculation is unspecified. These uncertainties prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
